<!-- generated by rfcspec-docs, do not edit -->

Checked against the design on 2026-11-04. RFCspec is at the design stage: 6 decisions, 7 planned milestones, nothing shipped. **Decided** is a decision in the design; **planned** is a milestone of the design's section 14 and nothing more.

| Area | Capability | Status | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design | [The catalogue, rfcspec/1](/docs/concepts/catalogue) | decided | An RFC becomes requirements, grammars, layouts, registries, defined procedures and limits, each with a source span and a digest (design D1). |
| Design | [ESS as the target](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | decided | Machines lower to ess-protospec/1, message and value types and registries to an ess/N system; what ESS cannot carry is listed as a gap (design D2). |
| Design | [A wire-format sidecar](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | decided | Bytes and bits live in rfcspec-wire/1: ABNF verbatim, bit-level ABNF and packet layouts (design D3). |
| Design | [Communication semantics](/docs/concepts/communication-semantics) | decided | One value per axis for each protocol layer: unit, delivery, direction, multiplexing, exchange, correlation, lifetime, layering, roles (design D4). |
| Design | [AI proposes, review decides](/docs/concepts/ai-proposals) | decided | Model output is a recorded proposal with cited spans, replayed offline; no gate calls a model (design D5, D6). |
| Design | [Which kinds of RFC are modelled](/docs/concepts/rfc-kinds) | decided | Wire protocols, data formats, extensions and registries are modelled; algorithms as signatures with test vectors; the rest get a requirement catalogue (design D11). |
| M0 Read | [Fetch, read and extract](/docs/design) | planned | RFC 6455 from plain text and RFC 9220 from RFCXML: sections, requirements, ABNF and defined terms; a survey classifying every RFC in the index by kind. |
| M1 Wire | [ABNF and the wire layer](/docs/examples/websocket) | planned | The RFC 6455 handshake grammar and frame bit-level ABNF and diagram, an agreement check between them, and a generated codec with round-trip and mutation vectors. |
| M2 Lower | [Proposals, review and lowering](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | planned | Recorded proposals for parties, semantics and the WebSocket machines, overlay review, and lowering that ess specify validate and ess protocol explore accept. |
| M3 Generate | [A generated WebSocket core](/docs/examples/websocket) | planned | A generated sans-IO Rust crate with codec, machine, limits and roles, an Autobahn run and the requirement matrix. |
| M4 DNS | [A second, binary protocol](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | planned | DNS over UDP: binary layouts, correlation by id, concurrent sessions; the ESS gap proposals with WebSocket and DNS as evidence. |
| M5 Spindle | [RFCspec cores in Spindle](/docs/concepts/lowering-to-ess) | planned | The WebSocket codec as a pure WASM module and a websocket channel port in a Spindle environment. |
| M6 TCP | [A transport](/docs/concepts/communication-semantics) | planned | TCP as the hard case: sequence-number arithmetic, windows and timers from measurements. |
